passages.source_text: Κλήμης Ἰακώβῳ τῷ κυρίῳ καὶ ἐπισκόπων ἐπισκόπῳ, διέποντι δὲ τὴν Ἱερουσαλὴμ ἁγίαν Ἑβραίων ἐκκλησίαν καὶ τὰς πανταχῇ θεοῦ προνοίᾳ ἱδρυθείσας καλῶς, σὺν τε πρεσβυτέροις καὶ διακόνοις καὶ τοῖς λοιποῖς ἅπασιν ἀδελφοῖς, εἰρήνη εἴη πάντοτε. γνώριμον ἔστω σοι, κύριέ μου, ὅτι Σίμων, ὁ διὰ τὴν ἀληθῆ πίστιν καὶ τὴν ἀσφαλεστάτην αὐτοῦ τῆς διδασκαλίας ὑπόθεσιν τῆς ἐκκλησίας θεμέλιος εἶναι ὁρισθεὶς καὶ δι’ αὐτὸ τοῦτο ὑπ’ αὐτοῦ τοῦ Ἰησοῦ ἀψευδεῖ στόματι μετονομασθεὶς Πέτρος, ἡ ἀπαρχὴ τοῦ κυρίου ἡμῶν, ὁ τῶν ἀποστόλων πρῶτος, ᾧ πρώτῳ ὁ πατὴρ τὸν υἱὸν ἀπεκάλυψεν, ὃν ὁ χριστὸς εὐλόγως ἐμακάρισεν, ὁ κλητὸς καὶ ἐκλεκτὸς καὶ συνέστιος καὶ συνοδίπορος, ὁ καλὸς καὶ δόκιμος μαθητής, ὁ τῆς δύσεως τὸ σκοτεινότερον τοῦ κόσμου μέρος ὡς πάντων ἱκανώτερος φωτίσαι κελευσθεὶς καὶ κατορθῶσαι δυνηθεὶς — καὶ δὴ μέχρι ποῦ· μηκύνω τὸν λόγον, μὴ βουλόμενος σημῆναι τὸ λυποῦν, ὃ ἐξ ἀνάγκης κἂν βραδὺ πάντως εἰπεῖν με δεῖ; — οὗτος αὐτὸς διὰ τὴν ἄμετρον πρὸς ἀνθρώπους στοργὴν σαφῶς δημοσία ἐπὶ τοῦ ἐνεστῶτος πονηροῦ τὸν ἐσόμενον ἀγαθὸν ὅλῳ τῷ κόσμῳ μηνύσας βασιλέα, μέχρις ἐνταῦθα τῆς Ῥώμης γενόμενος, θεοβουλήτῳ διδασκαλίᾳ σώζων ἀνθρώπους, αὐτὸς τοῦ νῦν βίου βιαίως τὸ ζῆν μετήλλαξεν.

πρὸς αὐταῖς δὲ ταῖς ἡμέραις αἷς ἤμελλεν τελευτᾶν, συνηθροισμένων τῶν ἀδελφῶν, αἰφνιδίως λαβόμενός μου τῆς χειρὸς ἐγερθεὶς ἐπὶ τῆς ἐκκλησίας ἔφη Ἀκούσατέ μου, ἀδελφοὶ καὶ σύνδουλοι. ἐπεὶ (ὡς ἐδιδάχθην ἀπὸ τοῦ με ἀποστείλαντος κυρίου τε καὶ διδασκάλου Ἰησοῦ χριστοῦ) αἱ τοῦ θανάτου μου ἠγγίκασιν ἡμέραι, Κλήμεντα τοῦτον ἐπίσκοπον ὑμῖν χειροτονῶ, ᾧ τὴν ἐμὴν τῶν λόγων πιστεύω καθέδραν, τῷ ἀπ’ ἀρχῆς μοι μέχρι τοῦ τέλους συνοδεύσαντι καὶ οὕτως πασῶν μου τῶν ὁμιλιῶν ἐπακούσαντι, συνελὼν ἐρῶ, ὃς ἐν πᾶσι πειρασμοῖς μου κοινωνήσας τῇ πίστει προσκαρτερῶν εὑρέθη, ὃν πλεῖον πάντων πεπείραμαι θεοσεβῆ, φιλάνθρωπον, ἁγνόν, πολυμαθῆ, σώφρονα, ἀγαθόν, δίκαιον, μακρόθυμον καὶ γενναίως εἰδότα φέρειν τὰς ἐνίων τῶν κατηχουμένων ἀχαριστίας. διὸ αὐτῷ μεταδίδωμι τὴν ἐξουσίαν τοῦ δεσμεύειν καὶ λύειν, ἵνα περὶ παντὸς οὗ ἂν χειροτονήσῃ ἐπὶ γῆς ἔσται δεδογματισμένον ἐν οὐρανοῖς. δήσει γὰρ ὃ δεῖ δεθῆναι, καὶ λύσει ὃ δεῖ λυθῆναι, ὡς τὸν τῆς ἐκκλησίας εἰδὼς κανόνα. αὐτοῦ οὖν ἀκούσατε ὡς γνόντες ὅτι ὁ τὸν ἀληθείας προκαθεζόμενον λυπῶν εἰς χριστὸν ἁμαρτάνει καὶ τὸν πατέρα τῶν ὅλων παροργίζει· οὗ εἵνεκεν οὐ ζήσεται. καὶ αὐτὸν οὖν δεῖ τὸν προκαθεζόμενον ἰατροῦ τόπον ἐπέχειν, οὐ θηρίου ἀλόγου θυμὸν ἔχειν.

αὐτοῦ ταῦτα λέγοντος ἐγὼ προσπεσὼν ἐδεόμην αὐτοῦ, παραιτούμενος τὴν τῆς καθέδρας τιμήν τε καὶ ἐξουσίαν. ὁ δ᾽. ἀπεκρίνατο Περὶ τούτου μή με ἀξίου· τοῦτο γὰρ γενέσθαι δέδοκταί μοι, καὶ ταύτῃ μᾶλλον εἰ παραιτῇ· ὅτι ἡ τοιαύτη καθέδρα οὐ φιλοκαθεδροῦντος τολμηροῦ χρείαν ἔχει, ἀλλ᾽ εὐλαβοῦς τὸν τρόπον καὶ πολυμαθοῦς τὸν λόγον. δὸς δὲ τὸν κρείττονα, ὃς ἐμοὶ σοῦ πλέον συνώδευσεν καὶ τῶν λόγων ἐπήκουσεν καὶ τὴν διοίκησιν τῆς ἐκκλησίας ἐκμεμάθηκεν, καὶ οὐκ ἀναγκάσω σε καλῶς ποιεῖν οὐ θέλοντα. ἀλλ᾽ οὐ δυνήσει νῦν τὸν σοῦ κρείττονα παρασχεῖν· σὺ γὰρ δι᾽ ἐμοῦ τῶν σωζομένων ἐθνῶν ἡ κρείττων ἀπαρχή. πλὴν καὶ τὸ ἕτερον λόγισαι ὅτι εἰ τὸν κίνδυνον τῆς ἁμαρτίας φοβούμενος οὐκ ἀναδέχῃ τῆς ἐκκλησίας τὴν διοίκησιν, εὖ ἴσθι εἰδὼς ὅτι πλεῖον ἁμαρτάνεις, ὅστις τοῖς θεοσεβέσιν ὥσπερ πλέουσιν καὶ κινδυνεύουσιν βοηθεῖν δυνάμενος οὐ θέλεις, διασκοπῶν μόνον τὸ ἴδιον καὶ οὐ τὸ κοινῇ πᾶσι συμφέρον. ὅτι δὲ τὸν κίνδυνον πάντως ἀναδέξασθαί σε δεῖ, ἐμοῦ τοῦτο ἀξιοῦν μὴ παυομένου εἰς τὴν τῶν πάντων βοήθειαν, ὀρθῶς ἐπίσταμαι. ὅσῳ οὖν μοι ταχύτερον συνευδοκήσεις, τοσοῦτόν με τῆς ἀθυμίας κουφίσεις.

οἶδα δὲ καὶ αὐτός, ὦ Κλήμης, λύπας καὶ ἀθυμίας καὶ κινδύνους καὶ ψόγους τοὺς ἐξ ἀπαιδεύτων ὄχλων σοι δωρούμενος, οὓς δυνήσει γενναίως φέρειν, ἐνορῶν τῆς ὑπομονῆς τὸν ἐκ θεοῦ σοι μέγαν ἀποδιδόμενον μισθόν. ἀλλὰ καὶ δικαίως συνενθυμήθητί μοι πότε σου τῆς ξυμμαχίας χρείαν ἔχει ὁ χριστός, νῦν ὅτε ὁ πονηρὸς κατὰ τῆς αὐτοῦ νύμφης πόλεμον ἤρατο, ἢ εἰς τὸν ἐπιόντα χρόνον ὅτε νικήσας βασιλεύει μηδεμιᾶς τοῦ λοιποῦ χρείαν ἔχων βοηθείας; οὐχὶ καὶ τῷ βραχὺ νοῦν ἔχοντι δῆλον ὅτι νῦν; πάσῃ οὖν προαιρέσει ἐν τῷ τῆς παρούσης ἀνάγκης χρόνῳ τάχυνον ξυμμαχῆσαι βασιλεῖ ἀγαθῷ, μισθοὺς μεγάλους· μετὰ νίκην ἀποδιδόναι πεφυκότι. χαίρων οὖν ἐπισκόπησον (εὐκαίρως ταύτῃ μᾶλλον ὡς διοίκησιν ἐκκλησίας παρ᾽ ἐμοῦ μεμαθηκώς) εἰς τὴν τῶν ἡμῖν προσφευγόντων ἀδελφῶν σωτηρίαν.

πλὴν καὶ βραχέα σε ἐπὶ πάντων διὰ πάντας τὰ τῆς διοικήσεως ὑπομνῆσαι θέλω. σὲ μὲν χρὴ ἀνεπιλήπτως βιοῦντα σπουδῇ μεγίστῃ πάσας τὰς τοῦ βίου ἀσχολίας ἀποσείεσθαι, μήτε ἐγγυητὴν γινόμενον μήτε συνήγορον μηδὲ ἑτέρῳ τινὶ βιωτικῷ παρεμπεπλεγμένον πράγματι. οὐ γὰρ κριτὴν καὶ δικαστὴν χρημάτων ἢ ἀσχολημάτων καθεστάναι σε θέλει τῶν νῦν βιωτικῶν πραγμάτων ὁ χριστός, ἵνα συνεχόμενος εἰς τὰς νῦν τῶν ἀνθρώπων φροντίδας μὴ εὐσχολῇς χωρίζειν λόγῳ ἀληθείας ἀνθρώπων τοὺς κρείττονας ἀπὸ τῶν χειρόνων. ἀλλὰ ταῦτα μὲν οἱ μανθάνοντες ἀλλήλοις παρεχέτωσαν , καὶ ἀπὸ τῶν σῴζειν δυναμένων λόγων μὴ ἀπασχολείτωσαν. ὡς γὰρ σοι ἀσεβές ἐστιν τὰς βιωτικὰς φροντίδας ἀναδέξασθαι καταλείψαντα ποιεῖν ὃ ἐκελεύσθης, οὕτως ἑκάστῳ λαϊκῷ ἁμαρτία ἐστίν, ἐὰν μὴ ἀλλήλοις καὶ ἐν ταῖς βιωτικαῖς χρείαις παρίστανται. καὶ σὲ δὲ περὶ ὧν χρὴ ἀμέριμνον εἶναι οἱ πάντες ποιεῖν ἐὰν μὴ νοῶσιν, παρὰ τῶν διακόνων μανθανέτωσαν, ἵνα μόνης τῆς ἐκκλησίας τὴν φροντίδα ἔχῃς, πρός τε τὸ διοικεῖν αὐτὴν καλῶς καὶ τὸ τοὺς τῆς ἀληθείας λόγους παρέχειν.

context.translation_policy_text:
# Translation Stance

This document states the translation commitments that guide every
decision in the People's Open Bible. Declaring them is an act of
honesty: critics can assess our output against our stated
commitments rather than guessing at hidden biases.

> **Status: first draft.** This document will be refined as the
> project matures. Input and disagreement are welcomed via GitHub
> issues.

## Theological stance

The People's Open Bible does not commit to a specific denominational
or creedal doctrinal stance. Where the source texts presuppose
theological claims — the divinity of Christ, the resurrection,
the personhood of the Holy Spirit, the unity of God — the
translation reflects those claims as the texts present them, not
as imposed commitments of the translator.

Readers from any tradition (Catholic, Eastern Orthodox, Protestant
of any stripe, non-denominational, inquirer) are invited to
evaluate POB against their own framework. Where a translation
decision is influenced by a theological reading — for example,
where a Greek construction is genuinely ambiguous and the English
choice leans one way or the other — that choice is documented in
the verse's `theological_decisions` block and the alternative
rendering is preserved in a footnote.

We do not pick sides on denominational distinctives (Reformed vs.
Arminian, infant vs. believer's baptism, real presence vs.
symbolic, cessationist vs. continuationist, etc.). Those questions
are for the reader and their faith community, not for the
translation.

## Translation philosophy

The People's Open Bible aims at **optimal equivalence**: the most faithful,
intelligible English representation of the source's meaning, wording patterns,
literary form, and rhetorical force. This is not an automatic midpoint between
formal and dynamic translation. Readability serves source fidelity; convention
and familiarity do not override it.

Specifically:

1. **Original-language primacy with reader-conscious wording.** Where
   long-standing English renderings obscure the source text's plain
   sense, we explain the source pressure openly. For *doulos*, the main
   text uses "servant" consistently while notes and the public audit
   trail preserve bonded-status, ownership, and total-allegiance nuance
   where it is historically or theologically salient (Rom 1:1, Phil 1:1).

2. **Translate titles; use conventional name forms.** Christological
   titles are translated to preserve meaning (*Christos* →
   "Messiah" when it functions independently as a title; *Kyrios* →
   "Lord"). In name-like constructions, use the familiar English forms
   "Jesus Christ" and "Christ Jesus." Personal names are otherwise
   transliterated by standard conventions. Thus "Jesus is the Messiah"
   retains the title, while Greek *Iēsous Christos* used as a personal-name
   construction is rendered "Jesus Christ."

3. **Preserve theological tension rather than resolve it.** Where
   the source is genuinely ambiguous on a contested interpretive
   question (e.g., *pistis Christou* — "faith in Christ" vs.
   "faithfulness of Christ"), we render one in the main text and
   preserve the alternative in a footnote, documenting the
   decision in the per-verse YAML.

4. **Consistency of key terms, or documented exception.** A given
   Greek or Hebrew word should receive a consistent English gloss
   across the translation, unless context demands variance — in
   which case the variance is documented per-verse with a
   rationale. The `consistency_lint.py` tool enforces this at
   commit time.

5. **Readable modern English, not archaic or academic.** The
   target reader is a literate 18–35-year-old English speaker.
   Vocabulary should be accessible without flattening theological
   weight. We avoid both ecclesiastical jargon ("propitiation" is
   footnoted, not required) and informality that undersells the
   text's gravity.

## Source distinctions and optimal English

Source fidelity takes priority over mere familiarity or defensibility. A
significant Greek or Hebrew wording pattern must receive an explicit comparison
with the best source-transparent English candidate, even when a prior draft
already discusses it in a footnote. Prior rationale is evidence, not a veto.
Do not infer different meanings from morphology alone or invent theology to
justify different glosses; preserve observable wording without adding claims.
A concise source-qualified or hyphenated rendering is available when ordinary
English otherwise conceals the source pattern. Record unresolved proposals for
maintainer review; do not silently certify them as unchanged or auto-publish.

**Approved scoped rendering:** John 21:15–17 uses **agape-love** for ἀγαπάω
and **phileo-love** for φιλέω, including the repeated question in verse 17.
The ἀγάπη noun's general table entry below is not a rule erasing that verb
pattern. Do not revert this approved POB/SPOB wording to generic “love”.

## Contested terms

The following terms appear frequently and carry heavy theological
weight. Our default rendering and rationale are recorded here.
Per-verse variance is documented in the individual YAML files.

| Greek / Hebrew | Default English | Alternatives considered | Rationale |
|---|---|---|---|
| Χριστός *Christos* | Messiah where independently titular; Christ in the name forms "Jesus Christ" / "Christ Jesus" | Christ, Messiah | Preserves the title's Hebraic messianic meaning while using the recognizable conventional English personal name |
| κύριος *Kyrios* | Lord | LORD, Master | Matches covenantal and NT usage |
| δοῦλος *doulos* | servant | bondservant, slave | Uses reader-facing "servant" consistently; documents bonded-status and ownership nuance in notes/audit metadata |
| πίστις *pistis* | faith | faithfulness, trust | Main text: faith; footnote alternatives where contested |
| δικαιοσύνη *dikaiosynē* | righteousness | justice | Both renderings preserved in footnotes for Pauline passages |
| ἱλαστήριον *hilastērion* | atoning sacrifice | propitiation, mercy seat | Dynamic rendering for accessibility; alternatives footnoted |
| ἀγάπη *agapē* | love | charity (archaic) | Lexical cognates in source kept |
| σάρξ *sarx* | flesh (literal) / sinful nature (metaphorical) | — | Context-dependent; per-verse documented |
| μετανοέω / μετάνοια *metanoeō / metanoia* | reorient / reorientation; toward God where the context warrants making the destination explicit | repent / repentance (traditional); reconsider / change of mind in documented exceptions | See "Reorientation terminology (2026-10-11)" below; do not homogenize regret, divine relenting, or distinct turning words |
| νήφω *nēphō* | clear-minded (most contexts); sober (where Paul explicitly runs the drunk/sober metaphor) | sober-minded | See revision notes in 1 Pet 5:8, 1 Thess 5:6 |
| יְהוָה YHWH | Yahweh | the LORD, Jehovah | Renders the divine name as a name. Where the NT quotes an OT YHWH passage using *Kyrios*, the NT verse retains "Lord" to preserve the Greek; the OT source verse uses "Yahweh". |
| אָדָם *adam* | man / humankind (context) | — | Context-dependent per usage |

## Reorientation terminology (2026-10-11)

Maintainer-approved English POB and SPOB reader wording uses **reorient /
reorientation** in place of the repent family for moral-spiritual redirection.
Use **toward God** when the context warrants making that direction explicit;
use **toward you** in direct prayer, and omit the extra destination when the
sentence already names it, supplies a departure from wrongdoing, or concerns
interpersonal reconsideration. Acts 20:21 explicitly supplies the Godward
phrase. The word *metanoia* by itself does not lexically contain "God."

This is an English editorial policy, not a claim that remorse is irrelevant or
that Greek word parts establish the full meaning. Preserve sorrow, named sins,
faith, forgiveness, and the distinction between a response and its fruit.
Keep separate turning expressions in Acts 3:19 and 26:20. Baptism's relationship
to reorientation must not be rewritten as "only symbolizes" or "causes."

**Context controls exceptions.** Retain regret, relenting, reconsideration,
change of mind, or turning back where that is the supported sense. Do not make
God reorient toward God; do not make a persecutor's demand for apostasy a call
toward God. Preserve contested interpretations in Job 42:6 and Hebrews 12:17.
Extra-canonical authors retain their own conceptual frameworks. Adapting a
historical English witness is not a new ancient-language translation, and must
be disclosed while its source transcription remains untouched.

**No invented intensifiers.** Do not add "fully," "completely," "radically,"
"truly," "wholeheartedly," or a superlative simply to strengthen reorientation.
Preserve such force only where the source supplies it. Hermas V.3.xiii.4
(reader chapter 21:4) has *holotelōs* and *ex holēs kardias*; its existing
"completely" and "from their whole heart" are not new additions.

Traditional terminology remains in alternative notes, original sources, and
historical revision records. Do not rewrite those layers to manufacture a
history of agreement. See [the application report](docs/REORIENTATION_POLICY_2026-10-11.md)
and the hash-bound plan in `config/terminology/`.

## What the translation is not

To prevent misunderstanding:

- **Not a paraphrase.** Every English rendering is tied to a
  specific source-text word or phrase, documented in the per-verse
  YAML.
- **Not a study Bible.** Footnotes document translation decisions,
  not doctrinal application or devotional commentary.
- **Not a denominational product.** The translation is
  intentionally cross-denominational. Contested readings are
  preserved in footnotes, not smoothed away.
- **Not a finalized translation.** Every verse is currently an
  AI-drafted rendering, released openly with full rationale. There
  is no formal scholarly review process at this time.
- **Not a first-century English approximation.** We aim at modern
  English that honors source-language meaning, not at archaism.

## Translating into other languages

The People's Open Bible's long-term intention is to be translated
into every major world language. Scripture belongs to the whole
church; producing POB only in English would contradict the
project's mission.

Each target language is its own translation — drafted directly
from the original-language sources (Hebrew OT, Greek NT, Swete
LXX for the deuterocanonical books) rather than from the English
POB. Translating from English would compound the distance from the
originals and inherit choices that make sense in English but not
elsewhere. Every target language deserves its own encounter with
the Hebrew and Greek.

Each language goes through **several revision passes** before it
is considered stable:

1. **AI-drafted first pass** — a frontier multilingual model
   produces the initial verse-by-verse draft with full per-verse
   provenance, following the same methodology used for English
   (DOCTRINE.md translation philosophy §§1–5, per-verse YAML
   schema, `doctrine_reference` citations where relevant).
2. **AI-reviewer revision** — a second, distinct model reads the
   draft and flags awkward phrasing, dropped nuance, or places
   where the target language's idiom has drifted from the
   source's force. Revisions are discrete commits.
3. **Native-speaker community review** — before a language is
   declared stable, speakers of that language who are also
   familiar with the biblical source languages (or who have
   access to published lexicons in that language) audit the
   text and raise issues publicly.
4. **Public issue window** — a minimum public-review period with
   open GitHub issues before any language moves from "preview"
   to "stable."

**Supported languages will be disclosed publicly based on model
performance and feasibility.** Not every language has an AI model
capable of scholarly-accurate translation yet, and not every
language has a sufficient community of native-speaking reviewers
accessible to the project. We will publish the current supported-
language list, and the ready-but-not-yet-stable list, as we reach
the capability threshold for each. Languages that do not yet meet
the bar are named as such, not silently omitted.

Every language published under this program carries the same
CC-BY 4.0 license, the same per-verse provenance, the same
auditability. There is no tier system across languages — every
supported language gets the full People's Open Bible.

## Change log for this document

Material changes to this document are themselves commits. Prior
versions of the stance are preserved in git history.

- **2026-04-21:** Removed creedal affirmations (Apostles' Creed,
  Nicene Creed, Chalcedonian Definition) and replaced with a
  theological-stance section that declines specific creedal
  commitment. Translation philosophy and contested-terms table
  preserved unchanged; those are methodology, not creedal
  commitment, and the project actually runs on them. Added a
  "Translating into other languages" section stating POB's long-
  term intention to ship in every feasible major language, with
  the full revision pipeline and transparent supported-language
  disclosure. Per-verse YAML citing the old `doctrine_reference`
  values is preserved as historical record; those are not
  retroactively edited.

Clement to James, the lord and bishop of bishops, who governs the holy Jerusalem church of the Hebrews and the churches everywhere that have been well established by God’s providence, together with the elders and deacons and all the other brothers: may peace always be.

Let it be known to you, my lord, that Simon—who, because of his true faith and the most secure basis of his teaching, was designated to be the foundation of the church and, for this very reason, was renamed Peter by Jesus himself with his unlying mouth; the firstfruits of our Lord; the first of the apostles; the one to whom the Father first revealed the Son; the one whom the Messiah rightly pronounced blessed; the called and chosen one, table companion and fellow traveler; the good and proven disciple; the one commanded to illuminate the West, the darker part of the world, as more capable than everyone else, and who proved able to accomplish it; and indeed, how long shall I prolong the account, unwilling to disclose the painful thing that necessity compels me, even if late, in any event to tell?—this same man, because of his boundless affection for humanity, having clearly and publicly proclaimed to the whole world, under the present evil one, the good king who was to come, and having come as far as here, to Rome, saving people through teaching willed by God, himself left this present life through violence.

lexical_decisions.chosen: the holy Jerusalem church of the Hebrews
lexical_decisions.rationale: Preserves Jerusalem as the church’s location or identifying designation and retains its explicit association with the Hebrews.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τὴν ἀσφαλεστάτην αὐτοῦ τῆς διδασκαλίας ὑπόθεσιν
lexical_decisions.chosen: the most secure basis of his teaching
lexical_decisions.rationale: Renders ὑπόθεσις as the underlying basis of the teaching and preserves the superlative force of ἀσφαλεστάτην.

lexical_decisions.chosen: with his unlying mouth
lexical_decisions.rationale: Keeps the source’s concrete image and its claim that Jesus’ naming was free from falsehood.

lexical_decisions.chosen: the Messiah
lexical_decisions.rationale: Χριστός functions independently as a title here rather than as part of the name Jesus Christ.

lexical_decisions.chosen: this same man
lexical_decisions.rationale: Marks the emphatic resumption of Simon after the extended series of descriptions and the intervening rhetorical question.

lexical_decisions.chosen: under the present evil one
lexical_decisions.rationale: With the genitive, ἐπί is taken temporally as locating the proclamation under the ascendancy of a personal evil figure; a more impersonal reading, ‘amid the present evil,’ remains possible.

lexical_decisions.chosen: through teaching willed by God
lexical_decisions.rationale: Renders θεοβούλητος as describing teaching that accords with or proceeds from God’s will.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τοῦ νῦν βίου βιαίως τὸ ζῆν μετήλλαξεν
lexical_decisions.chosen: left this present life through violence
lexical_decisions.rationale: Communicates the death denoted by the exchange-language while retaining the explicit claim that the departure from life was violent; μετήλλαξεν literally depicts an exchange or change, without naming what was received in exchange.

source_issues.source_quote: καὶ δὴ μέχρι ποῦ· μηκύνω τὸν λόγον, μὴ βουλόμενος σημῆναι τὸ λυποῦν, ὃ ἐξ ἀνάγκης κἂν βραδὺ πάντως εἰπεῖν με δεῖ;
source_issues.issue: The printed high point after μέχρι ποῦ interrupts the interrogative phrase from its verb μηκύνω, leaving the exact scope of the rhetorical question editorially uncertain. The translation provisionally takes the words together as a rhetorical interruption within the larger sentence about Simon; the punctuation is a confirmed editorial feature, not evidence of source corruption.
source_issues.proposed_reading: καὶ δὴ μέχρι ποῦ μηκύνω τὸν λόγον, μὴ βουλόμενος σημῆναι τὸ λυποῦν, ὃ ἐξ ἀνάγκης κἂν βραδὺ πάντως εἰπεῖν με δεῖ;

passages.text: Now, in the very days when he was about to die, after the brothers had assembled, he suddenly took hold of my hand, stood up before the church, and said, “Listen to me, brothers and fellow servants. Since—as I was taught by the Lord and Teacher Jesus Christ, who sent me—the days of my death have drawn near, I ordain this Clement as bishop for you. To him I entrust my chair of teaching. He accompanied me from the beginning to the end and thus listened to all my discourses; to speak in summary, he shared in all my trials and was found persevering in faith. More than anyone else, I have found by experience that he is God-revering, a lover of humanity, pure, widely learned, self-controlled, good, just, patient, and knows how to bear bravely the acts of ingratitude committed by some of those receiving instruction. Therefore I impart to him the authority to bind and release, so that, concerning whatever he ordains on earth, it will stand decreed in the heavens. For he will bind what must be bound and release what must be released, since he knows the church’s rule. Listen to him, therefore, recognizing that whoever grieves the one who presides over truth sins against the Messiah and provokes the Father of all; for this reason, that person will not live. Therefore the one who presides must himself occupy the place of a physician, not possess the rage of an irrational beast.”

lexical_decisions.chosen: fellow servants
lexical_decisions.rationale: Retains the shared servant status expressed by the compound rather than reducing it to a general term for colleagues.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ᾧ τὴν ἐμὴν τῶν λόγων πιστεύω καθέδραν
lexical_decisions.chosen: To him I entrust my chair of teaching
lexical_decisions.rationale: Preserves the institutional chair image while taking τῶν λόγων to characterize it as the chair associated with Peter’s words or teaching.

lexical_decisions.chosen: to speak in summary
lexical_decisions.rationale: Conveys the idiom’s transition from the preceding details to a concise characterization.

lexical_decisions.chosen: a lover of humanity
lexical_decisions.rationale: Preserves the word’s explicit orientation toward human beings rather than narrowing it to generic kindness.

lexical_decisions.chosen: those receiving instruction
lexical_decisions.rationale: Conveys the participle’s sense without requiring the later technical loanword ‘catechumens.’

lexical_decisions.chosen: to bind and release
lexical_decisions.rationale: Keeps the paired judicial and disciplinary imagery while distinguishing λύειν from merely untying a physical object.

lexical_decisions.chosen: concerning whatever he ordains
lexical_decisions.rationale: Restores the explicit περὶ, ‘concerning,’ and keeps χειροτονέω visibly connected with the earlier ‘I ordain.’ The phrase may instead refer personally to ‘anyone he appoints.’

lexical_decisions.chosen: it will stand decreed in the heavens
lexical_decisions.rationale: Preserves the established-decree sense of δεδογματισμένον without directly identifying the object of Clement’s earthly action with the heavenly decree.

lexical_decisions.chosen: occupy the place of a physician
lexical_decisions.rationale: Retains the contrast between healing authority and the rage of an irrational beast.

source_issues.source_quote: ἵνα περὶ παντὸς οὗ ἂν χειροτονήσῃ ἐπὶ γῆς ἔσται δεδογματισμένον ἐν οὐρανοῖς
source_issues.issue: The gender and reference of παντὸς οὗ and the semantic range of χειροτονέω permit both an impersonal interpretation, ‘concerning whatever he ordains on earth,’ and a personal interpretation, ‘concerning anyone he appoints on earth.’ The main translation provisionally adopts the former while preserving περὶ and the recurrence of the ordination verb; neither interpretation is uniquely established by the supplied wording.

passages.text: As he was saying these things, I fell before him and pleaded with him, declining the honor and authority of the chair. But he answered, “Do not ask this of me, for I have resolved that this should happen—and all the more for this very reason, if you decline it—because such a chair does not need a rash man eager to occupy the chair, but one who is circumspect in character and widely learned in discourse. Produce someone better, one who accompanied me more than you, listened to my words, and thoroughly learned the governance of the church, and I will not force you, against your will, to do what is right. But you will not now be able to produce anyone better than yourself, for you are the superior firstfruit of the nations being saved through me. Nevertheless, consider this other point as well: if, fearing the danger of sin, you do not undertake the governance of the church, know well that you sin more, since, though able to help those who revere God, as people sailing and in danger, you refuse, considering only your own interest and not what benefits everyone in common. I know with certainty that you must in every case undertake the danger, since I do not cease asking this of you for the help of everyone. Therefore, the sooner you agree with me, the more you will relieve me of discouragement.”

lexical_decisions.source_quote: παραιτούμενος τὴν τῆς καθέδρας τιμήν τε καὶ ἐξουσίαν
lexical_decisions.chosen: declining the honor and authority of the chair
lexical_decisions.rationale: Preserves Clement’s refusal of both the office’s honor and its governing power.

lexical_decisions.chosen: a rash man eager to occupy the chair
lexical_decisions.rationale: Conveys the coined expression’s criticism of someone recklessly ambitious for the presiding seat.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: εὐλαβοῦς τὸν τρόπον καὶ πολυμαθοῦς τὸν λόγον
lexical_decisions.chosen: circumspect in character and widely learned in discourse
lexical_decisions.rationale: The context contrasts reckless ambition with cautious character and extensive competence in teaching or discourse.

lexical_decisions.chosen: Produce someone better
lexical_decisions.rationale: The imperative challenges Clement to supply a more qualified alternative, continuing the comparative language of κρείττων.

lexical_decisions.chosen: the superior firstfruit
lexical_decisions.rationale: Retains κρείττων as a comparative description rather than converting it into an English superlative; ‘more excellent firstfruit’ is a possible alternative.

lexical_decisions.chosen: as people sailing and in danger
lexical_decisions.rationale: Retains both the maritime action and the accompanying danger.

lexical_decisions.chosen: what benefits everyone in common
lexical_decisions.rationale: Preserves the contrast between Clement’s private interest and the community’s shared good.

lexical_decisions.chosen: you agree with me
lexical_decisions.rationale: The compound describes Clement joining Peter in approving and accepting the proposed course.

source_issues.issue: The supplied print places a full stop immediately after the elided δ᾽, syntactically separating ὁ δ᾽ from ἀπεκρίνατο. The translation provisionally reads the words continuously as ‘But he answered.’ This appears to be an editorial punctuation blemish, not evidence of missing text.

source_issues.source_quote: σὺ γὰρ δι᾽ ἐμοῦ τῶν σωζομένων ἐθνῶν ἡ κρείττων ἀπαρχή
source_issues.issue: The attachment of δι᾽ ἐμοῦ is interpretively uncertain. The translation connects it with σωζομένων, yielding ‘the nations being saved through me.’ It can instead modify the main assertion: ‘through me you are the superior firstfruit of the nations being saved.’ The supplied wording requires no textual correction.

passages.text: “I myself also know, Clement, that I am bestowing on you griefs, discouragements, dangers, and reproaches from uneducated crowds. You will be able to bear these bravely by keeping in view the great reward from God that will be repaid to you for your endurance. But also, as is right, consider together with me: when does the Messiah need your alliance—now, when the evil one has taken up war against his bride, or in the coming time, when, having conquered, he reigns and no longer needs any help? Is it not clear even to someone with little understanding that it is now? Therefore, with full resolve, hurry in this present time of need to ally yourself with a good king, whose nature it is to repay great rewards after victory. Gladly, then, exercise oversight—all the more suitably in this respect, since you have learned from me how to govern the church—for the salvation of the brothers who flee to us for refuge.”

lexical_decisions.chosen: I am bestowing on you
lexical_decisions.rationale: Uses a single gift-related verb for Peter’s act and keeps the griefs, dangers, and reproaches as its objects; the verb pointedly presents the imposed burdens as things bestowed.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ἐνορῶν τῆς ὑπομονῆς τὸν ἐκ θεοῦ σοι μέγαν ἀποδιδόμενον μισθόν
lexical_decisions.chosen: keeping in view the great reward from God that will be repaid to you for your endurance
lexical_decisions.rationale: Preserves the visual orientation of ἐνορῶν and the recompense language of μισθός and ἀποδίδωμι.

lexical_decisions.chosen: the Messiah
lexical_decisions.rationale: Χριστός functions independently as the title of the king whose cause Clement is urged to support.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: κατὰ τῆς αὐτοῦ νύμφης πόλεμον ἤρατο
lexical_decisions.chosen: has taken up war against his bride
lexical_decisions.rationale: Keeps both the military action and the bride image without identifying the bride more explicitly than the source does.

lexical_decisions.chosen: Therefore, with full resolve
lexical_decisions.rationale: Προαίρεσις denotes deliberate purpose or resolve, while πάσῃ supplies the comprehensive force represented by ‘full.’

lexical_decisions.chosen: to ally yourself with a good king
lexical_decisions.rationale: Preserves the political and military alliance imagery rather than generalizing it as mere assistance.

lexical_decisions.chosen: whose nature it is to repay
lexical_decisions.rationale: Conveys πεφυκότι as an established disposition or characteristic of the good king.

lexical_decisions.chosen: Gladly, then, exercise oversight
lexical_decisions.rationale: The verb calls Clement to perform episcopal oversight and retains its word-family connection with ἐπίσκοπος without forcing an English denominational formulation.

lexical_decisions.chosen: the brothers who flee to us for refuge
lexical_decisions.rationale: Retains the directional movement and protective force of προσφεύγω.

source_issues.source_quote: μισθοὺς μεγάλους· μετὰ νίκην ἀποδιδόναι πεφυκότι
source_issues.issue: The printed high point places a strong editorial pause between the object μισθοὺς μεγάλους and the infinitive ἀποδιδόναι on which it depends. The syntax remains recoverable, and the translation provisionally reads the phrase continuously. The proposed reading is conjectural repunctuation only.
source_issues.proposed_reading: μισθοὺς μεγάλους μετὰ νίκην ἀποδιδόναι πεφυκότι

passages.text: “Nevertheless, before everyone and for everyone’s sake, I also wish to remind you briefly about the matters of governance. You must live blamelessly and, with the greatest diligence, shake off all the occupations of life, becoming neither a guarantor nor an advocate and becoming entangled in no other worldly affair. For the Messiah does not want you appointed as a judge and adjudicator over money or business among the present affairs of worldly life and thereby, absorbed in people’s present concerns, left without leisure to separate, by the word of truth, the better people from the worse. Rather, let those who are learning provide these things for one another, and let them not distract you from the words capable of saving. For just as it is impious for you to undertake worldly concerns while neglecting to do what you were commanded, so it is a sin for each layperson if they do not stand by one another also in worldly needs. Moreover, if all of them do not understand about which matters they ought to keep you free from concern, let them learn from the deacons, so that you may care only for the church, both governing it well and providing the words of truth.”

lexical_decisions.chosen: before everyone and for everyone’s sake
lexical_decisions.rationale: Takes ἐπὶ πάντων as indicating the public setting and διὰ πάντας as expressing the concern for everyone that motivates the instruction.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: πάσας τὰς τοῦ βίου ἀσχολίας ἀποσείεσθαι
lexical_decisions.chosen: shake off all the occupations of life
lexical_decisions.rationale: Retains the physical force of ἀποσείω and the comprehensive scope of πάσας.

lexical_decisions.chosen: becoming neither a guarantor nor an advocate
lexical_decisions.rationale: Preserves the distinct financial and legal roles prohibited to the bishop.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: κριτὴν καὶ δικαστὴν χρημάτων ἢ ἀσχολημάτων
lexical_decisions.chosen: a judge and adjudicator over money or business
lexical_decisions.rationale: Distinguishes the two judicial terms while treating χρημάτων and ἀσχολημάτων as the financial and business matters over which judgment would be exercised.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: χωρίζειν λόγῳ ἀληθείας ἀνθρώπων τοὺς κρείττονας ἀπὸ τῶν χειρόνων
lexical_decisions.chosen: to separate, by the word of truth, the better people from the worse
lexical_decisions.rationale: Retains the source’s language of separation and its comparison between better and worse persons.

lexical_decisions.chosen: those who are learning
lexical_decisions.rationale: Keeps the expression broader than a fixed institutional label such as ‘catechumens.’

lexical_decisions.chosen: for each layperson
lexical_decisions.rationale: Λαϊκός distinguishes an ordinary member from the bishop and deacons in the surrounding instructions.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: περὶ ὧν χρὴ ἀμέριμνον εἶναι οἱ πάντες ποιεῖν
lexical_decisions.chosen: about which matters they ought to keep you free from concern
lexical_decisions.rationale: Keeps the freedom specifically as freedom from concern about the matters, not freedom from the matters themselves. The placement of χρὴ also permits taking the necessity as applying directly to Clement’s being free from concern.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: μόνης τῆς ἐκκλησίας τὴν φροντίδα ἔχῃς
lexical_decisions.chosen: you may care only for the church
lexical_decisions.rationale: Preserves the exclusive force of μόνης and the church as the bishop’s assigned sphere of concern.

source_issues.source_quote: οὐ γὰρ κριτὴν καὶ δικαστὴν χρημάτων ἢ ἀσχολημάτων καθεστάναι σε θέλει τῶν νῦν βιωτικῶν πραγμάτων ὁ χριστός, ἵνα συνεχόμενος εἰς τὰς νῦν τῶν ἀνθρώπων φροντίδας μὴ εὐσχολῇς χωρίζειν λόγῳ ἀληθείας ἀνθρώπων τοὺς κρείττονας ἀπὸ τῶν χειρόνων
source_issues.issue: The scope of the unusual οὐ ... θέλει ... ἵνα ... μὴ construction is interpretively difficult. The translation takes the ἵνα clause as the unwanted outcome included within the Messiah’s negated desire: appointment to worldly adjudication would absorb Clement and leave him without leisure for his teaching task. A more formally sequential rendering with ‘so that’ could obscure this scope or suggest that the lack of leisure is the purpose of refusing the appointment. No textual correction is proposed.

source_issues.source_quote: καὶ σὲ δὲ περὶ ὧν χρὴ ἀμέριμνον εἶναι οἱ πάντες ποιεῖν ἐὰν μὴ νοῶσιν, παρὰ τῶν διακόνων μανθανέτωσαν
source_issues.issue: The marked word order leaves the relationship of χρὴ to ἀμέριμνον εἶναι and ποιεῖν interpretively uncertain. The translation provisionally understands the necessity as governing the community’s keeping Clement free from concern about certain matters. Alternatively, the phrase may mean that Clement himself ought to be free from concern about those matters and that, if all do not know how to make him so, they should learn from the deacons. This is a syntactic ambiguity in the supplied wording, not evidence of missing or corrupt text.

## Theological stance

The People's Open Bible does not commit to a specific denominational
or creedal doctrinal stance. Where the source texts presuppose
theological claims — the divinity of Christ, the resurrection,
the personhood of the Holy Spirit, the unity of God — the
translation reflects those claims as the texts present them, not
as imposed commitments of the translator.

Readers from any tradition (Catholic, Eastern Orthodox, Protestant
of any stripe, non-denominational, inquirer) are invited to
evaluate POB against their own framework. Where a translation
decision is influenced by a theological reading — for example,
where a Greek construction is genuinely ambiguous and the English
choice leans one way or the other — that choice is documented in
the verse's `theological_decisions` block and the alternative
rendering is preserved in a footnote.

We do not pick sides on denominational distinctives (Reformed vs.
Arminian, infant vs. believer's baptism, real presence vs.
symbolic, cessationist vs. continuationist, etc.). Those questions
are for the reader and their faith community, not for the
translation.

## Translation philosophy

The People's Open Bible aims at **optimal equivalence**: the most faithful,
intelligible English representation of the source's meaning, wording patterns,
literary form, and rhetorical force. This is not an automatic midpoint between
formal and dynamic translation. Readability serves source fidelity; convention
and familiarity do not override it.

Specifically:

1. **Original-language primacy with reader-conscious wording.** Where
   long-standing English renderings obscure the source text's plain
   sense, we explain the source pressure openly. For *doulos*, the main
   text uses "servant" consistently while notes and the public audit
   trail preserve bonded-status, ownership, and total-allegiance nuance
   where it is historically or theologically salient (Rom 1:1, Phil 1:1).

2. **Translate titles; use conventional name forms.** Christological
   titles are translated to preserve meaning (*Christos* →
   "Messiah" when it functions independently as a title; *Kyrios* →
   "Lord"). In name-like constructions, use the familiar English forms
   "Jesus Christ" and "Christ Jesus." Personal names are otherwise
   transliterated by standard conventions. Thus "Jesus is the Messiah"
   retains the title, while Greek *Iēsous Christos* used as a personal-name
   construction is rendered "Jesus Christ."

3. **Preserve theological tension rather than resolve it.** Where
   the source is genuinely ambiguous on a contested interpretive
   question (e.g., *pistis Christou* — "faith in Christ" vs.
   "faithfulness of Christ"), we render one in the main text and
   preserve the alternative in a footnote, documenting the
   decision in the per-verse YAML.

4. **Consistency of key terms, or documented exception.** A given
   Greek or Hebrew word should receive a consistent English gloss
   across the translation, unless context demands variance — in
   which case the variance is documented per-verse with a
   rationale. The `consistency_lint.py` tool enforces this at
   commit time.

5. **Readable modern English, not archaic or academic.** The
   target reader is a literate 18–35-year-old English speaker.
   Vocabulary should be accessible without flattening theological
   weight. We avoid both ecclesiastical jargon ("propitiation" is
   footnoted, not required) and informality that undersells the
   text's gravity.

## Source distinctions and optimal English

Source fidelity takes priority over mere familiarity or defensibility. A
significant Greek or Hebrew wording pattern must receive an explicit comparison
with the best source-transparent English candidate, even when a prior draft
already discusses it in a footnote. Prior rationale is evidence, not a veto.
Do not infer different meanings from morphology alone or invent theology to
justify different glosses; preserve observable wording without adding claims.
A concise source-qualified or hyphenated rendering is available when ordinary
English otherwise conceals the source pattern. Record unresolved proposals for
maintainer review; do not silently certify them as unchanged or auto-publish.

**Approved scoped rendering:** John 21:15–17 uses **agape-love** for ἀγαπάω
and **phileo-love** for φιλέω, including the repeated question in verse 17.
The ἀγάπη noun's general table entry below is not a rule erasing that verb
pattern. Do not revert this approved POB/SPOB wording to generic “love”.

## Reorientation terminology (2026-10-11)

Maintainer-approved English POB and SPOB reader wording uses **reorient /
reorientation** in place of the repent family for moral-spiritual redirection.
Use **toward God** when the context warrants making that direction explicit;
use **toward you** in direct prayer, and omit the extra destination when the
sentence already names it, supplies a departure from wrongdoing, or concerns
interpersonal reconsideration. Acts 20:21 explicitly supplies the Godward
phrase. The word *metanoia* by itself does not lexically contain "God."

This is an English editorial policy, not a claim that remorse is irrelevant or
that Greek word parts establish the full meaning. Preserve sorrow, named sins,
faith, forgiveness, and the distinction between a response and its fruit.
Keep separate turning expressions in Acts 3:19 and 26:20. Baptism's relationship
to reorientation must not be rewritten as "only symbolizes" or "causes."

**Context controls exceptions.** Retain regret, relenting, reconsideration,
change of mind, or turning back where that is the supported sense. Do not make
God reorient toward God; do not make a persecutor's demand for apostasy a call
toward God. Preserve contested interpretations in Job 42:6 and Hebrews 12:17.
Extra-canonical authors retain their own conceptual frameworks. Adapting a
historical English witness is not a new ancient-language translation, and must
be disclosed while its source transcription remains untouched.

**No invented intensifiers.** Do not add "fully," "completely," "radically,"
"truly," "wholeheartedly," or a superlative simply to strengthen reorientation.
Preserve such force only where the source supplies it. Hermas V.3.xiii.4
(reader chapter 21:4) has *holotelōs* and *ex holēs kardias*; its existing
"completely" and "from their whole heart" are not new additions.

Traditional terminology remains in alternative notes, original sources, and
historical revision records. Do not rewrite those layers to manufacture a
history of agreement. See [the application report](docs/REORIENTATION_POLICY_2026-10-11.md)
and the hash-bound plan in `config/terminology/`.

## What the translation is not

To prevent misunderstanding:

- **Not a paraphrase.** Every English rendering is tied to a
  specific source-text word or phrase, documented in the per-verse
  YAML.
- **Not a study Bible.** Footnotes document translation decisions,
  not doctrinal application or devotional commentary.
- **Not a denominational product.** The translation is
  intentionally cross-denominational. Contested readings are
  preserved in footnotes, not smoothed away.
- **Not a finalized translation.** Every verse is currently an
  AI-drafted rendering, released openly with full rationale. There
  is no formal scholarly review process at this time.
- **Not a first-century English approximation.** We aim at modern
  English that honors source-language meaning, not at archaism.

## Translating into other languages

The People's Open Bible's long-term intention is to be translated
into every major world language. Scripture belongs to the whole
church; producing POB only in English would contradict the
project's mission.

Each target language is its own translation — drafted directly
from the original-language sources (Hebrew OT, Greek NT, Swete
LXX for the deuterocanonical books) rather than from the English
POB. Translating from English would compound the distance from the
originals and inherit choices that make sense in English but not
elsewhere. Every target language deserves its own encounter with
the Hebrew and Greek.

Each language goes through **several revision passes** before it
is considered stable:

1. **AI-drafted first pass** — a frontier multilingual model
   produces the initial verse-by-verse draft with full per-verse
   provenance, following the same methodology used for English
   (DOCTRINE.md translation philosophy §§1–5, per-verse YAML
   schema, `doctrine_reference` citations where relevant).
2. **AI-reviewer revision** — a second, distinct model reads the
   draft and flags awkward phrasing, dropped nuance, or places
   where the target language's idiom has drifted from the
   source's force. Revisions are discrete commits.
3. **Native-speaker community review** — before a language is
   declared stable, speakers of that language who are also
   familiar with the biblical source languages (or who have
   access to published lexicons in that language) audit the
   text and raise issues publicly.
4. **Public issue window** — a minimum public-review period with
   open GitHub issues before any language moves from "preview"
   to "stable."

**Supported languages will be disclosed publicly based on model
performance and feasibility.** Not every language has an AI model
capable of scholarly-accurate translation yet, and not every
language has a sufficient community of native-speaking reviewers
accessible to the project. We will publish the current supported-
language list, and the ready-but-not-yet-stable list, as we reach
the capability threshold for each. Languages that do not yet meet
the bar are named as such, not silently omitted.

Every language published under this program carries the same
CC-BY 4.0 license, the same per-verse provenance, the same
auditability. There is no tier system across languages — every
supported language gets the full People's Open Bible.
